newsitem.title: UK: UK proposes pension splitting on divorce.
newsitem.headline: UK proposes pension splitting on divorce.

text.p: The British government unveiled proposals on Wednesday that would allow for the first time pension rights to be split when a couple divorces.
Thousands of divorcees, mainly women, could benefit from the proposed changes.

But a white policy paper issued by the Department of Social Security said splitting would not be automatic in every case, the pension rights need not be divided 50-50, and splitting would apply to both men and women.
It would be up to the courts to decide whether splitting is approriate and, if so, the terms.
"The availability of pension splitting will provide greater flexibility to reach a fair divorce settlement," junior minister Lord MacKay of Ardbrecknish said in a statement.
"But splitting will not be required in every divorce. Pensions are just one of the assets the court will consider in the financial settlement," he added.

The government said it was committed to introducing primary legislation as sson as practicable but stressed that, as splitting rights is a new departure in pension provision, detailed and complex amendments would be required to a range of laws and pension rules.
The opposition Labour party accused the government of foot-dragging and estimated that 150,000 women could lose out for every year's delay in introducing pension splitting.
